questions.scenario: When you were younger (or even now) and a toy or gadget broke, what did you usually do?

options.text: Take it apart to look at the physical gears, springs, and moving parts.
Fascinated by the green circuit boards, wires, and tiny chips inside.
Plug it into a computer to see if I could hack or reset the software.
Think about how it could have been designed better so it wouldn't break in the first place.

questions.scenario: Your school is participating in a major Science Fair. What project do you choose?

options.text: Building a working hydraulic crane or a mechanical walking spider.
Creating a smart security alarm by soldering sensors, lasers, and buzzers together.
Writing the code for a self-driving toy car that can perfectly follow a black line.
Designing a cool, wearable smart-watch concept that solves a problem for students.

questions.scenario: You are watching Iron Man. What part of his suit fascinates you the most?

options.text: The mechanical thrusters, armor plating, and how the suit physically folds out.
The Arc Reactor power source and the internal wiring that connects everything.
JARVIS—the artificial intelligence that controls the targeting and voice commands.
The sleek visual design and how Tony Stark continuously upgrades his tech empire.

questions.scenario: A brand new gaming console (like the PS5 or Xbox) just dropped. What YouTube video do you watch about it?

options.text: A video showing the physical cooling fan system and the case design.
A complete 'teardown' video showing the custom motherboard and CPU chips.
A video testing the new software dashboard and game engine physics.
A review discussing its price, marketing strategy, and if it will beat the competition.

questions.scenario: You join the school's robotics club. How do you divide the work?

options.text: I'll build the chassis, attach the wheels, and make sure it is physically strong.
I'll handle the battery connections, wiring, and plugging in the motor controllers.
I'll sit with my laptop and write the Python or C++ code to make it move.
I'll lead the team, manage the budget, and pitch our robot to the judges.

questions.scenario: If you could instantly download a new technical skill into your brain, what would it be?

options.text: Mastering 3D modeling software (like AutoCAD) to design mechanical parts.
The ability to perfectly solder microchips and design complex circuit boards.
Fluency in three different programming languages instantly.
The ability to know exactly what kind of gadget millions of people want to buy.

questions.scenario: You are looking at a smart home device, like an Amazon Echo or Google Nest. What do you wonder about?

options.text: How they designed the acoustic shape of the speaker to project sound so well.
How the tiny microphone arrays inside capture audio from across the room.
How the machine learning algorithm understands my specific voice accent.
What new features they could add next year to make me buy the upgraded version.

questions.scenario: Your TV remote stops working. After changing the batteries, it still doesn't work. What is your next move?

options.text: Check if a button is physically jammed or the plastic casing is broken.
Open it up to see if a wire snapped or the battery contacts are rusted.
Try to find the manual online to see if there's a button combination to factory reset it.
Give up, complain about how badly it's designed, and look for a universal remote online.

questions.scenario: You are watching a sci-fi movie featuring a giant walking robot. What is your reaction?

options.text: 'Those hydraulic legs are amazing, I wonder how they support all that weight.'
'Where are the power cables? That thing would need a massive battery pack!'
'I wonder how complex the sensors are to keep it from falling over.'
'If they sold remote-control mini versions of that, they would make billions.'

questions.scenario: What is the best compliment someone could give you on a tech project?

options.text: 'This is built like a tank. The physical design is flawless and super durable.'
'Your wiring is incredibly neat, and the circuit works perfectly on the first try.'
'Your code is so elegant! The robot reacts so smoothly and intelligently.'
'This is genius. I would honestly pay ₹5000 to buy this right now.'

Robotics_Engineer.title: Mechanical / Robotics Engineer
Robotics_Engineer.primary_match_text: You are a builder at heart. You love understanding how things physically move, you think in 3D, and you enjoy working with gears, motors, and structures.
Robotics_Engineer.day_in_the_life: Designing the physical chassis of a robot in 3D software (like AutoCAD), testing motors, and building machines that can lift, walk, or fly in the real world.
Robotics_Engineer.alternative_match_text: Because you love understanding how physical forces work, a career in Automobile Engineering or Aerospace Engineering is also a fantastic fit.
Robotics_Engineer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or Robotics. Learn CAD and 3D printing.

Electronics_Engineer.title: Electronics & Hardware Engineer
Electronics_Engineer.primary_match_text: You are the 'brain surgeon' of machines. You are fascinated by electricity, circuit boards, and microchips—the hidden components that give gadgets power.
Electronics_Engineer.day_in_the_life: Designing custom green circuit boards (PCBs), soldering microscopic sensors, and making sure power flows safely from the battery to the processors.
Electronics_Engineer.alternative_match_text: Since you have a great eye for detail and circuits, working as a Telecommunications Engineer or a Semiconductor Designer is a highly paid backup plan.
Electronics_Engineer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Electronics & Communication Engineering (ECE) or Electrical Engineering. Practice with Arduino or Raspberry Pi.

Automation_Programmer.title: Robotics Software / AI Engineer
Automation_Programmer.primary_match_text: You are the logic master. You don't just want to build a machine; you want to make it smart. You love coding, problem-solving, and making devices think for themselves.
Automation_Programmer.day_in_the_life: Writing complex algorithms in Python or C++ that take data from cameras and sensors, allowing a drone to dodge trees or a self-driving car to stop at a red light.
Automation_Programmer.alternative_match_text: Because you have strong coding and logic skills, shifting entirely to Software Engineering or Artificial Intelligence is an easy and lucrative alternative.
Automation_Programmer.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) with Computer Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Computer Science or AI & Machine Learning. Master languages like C++ and Python.

Hardware_Product_Manager.title: Tech Entrepreneur / Hardware Product Manager
Hardware_Product_Manager.primary_match_text: You are the visionary. You look at technology and immediately think about the consumer. You understand what people want to buy and how a product should look and feel.
Hardware_Product_Manager.day_in_the_life: Looking at a team of engineers and saying, 'Make the battery smaller so the phone looks sleeker,' then pitching the final product to investors or the public.
Hardware_Product_Manager.alternative_match_text: With your mix of technical understanding and business sense, a career in Tech Sales or working as a Startup Founder is a perfect path for you.
Hardware_Product_Manager.roadmap: Take Commerce or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA in Tech Management, or a B.Tech followed by an MBA. Focus on product design and business strategy.
